service_boundary: Represents model inference and deployment in Microsoft Foundry, including Azure OpenAI as an Azure-hosted path, not the direct OpenAI API, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or the broader Foundry agent platform.
regional_controls: Standard, Global, and Data Zone deployments have different processing boundaries. Geography-scoped and EU, US, or APAC Data Zone options are model- and deployment-specific.
retention_controls: Microsoft states Azure Direct Model prompts and outputs are not shared with model providers or used to train foundation models without permission; stateful APIs, batch, files, and abuse monitoring have separate storage behavior.
routing: Global and Data Zone deployment types can route capacity across allowed Azure locations for the selected model; this is cloud-capacity routing, not general provider selection.
customization: Fine-tuning, provisioned deployments, managed compute, and customer model deployments are available for eligible models.
strengths: A large multi-publisher catalog is integrated with Azure identity, networking, and geography controls.
Common inference APIs reduce integration differences across supported models.
tradeoffs: Model availability, terms, and processing geography vary by deployment type.
The product boundary and naming evolve quickly and require careful distinction from direct vendor APIs.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the model appears in the API reference or the security documentation.
response_integrity.scope: Azure AI Foundry model inference API reference, for Microsoft Foundry Models

upstream_disclosure.note: The data-privacy page states who does and does not receive content: prompts, completions, embeddings, and training data "are NOT available to OpenAI or other providers of Models sold by Azure", and "Microsoft hosts the Models sold by Azure in Microsoft's Azure environment and Models sold by Azure do NOT interact with any services operated by providers of Models sold by Azure".
upstream_disclosure.scope: Azure Foundry data, privacy, and security page, for Microsoft Foundry Models

credential_handling.note: The service offers no customer-supplied-key path: "Each request to Foundry Tools must include an authentication header. This header passes along a resource key or authentication token, which is used to validate your subscription for a service or group of services."
credential_handling.scope: Azure AI services authentication page, for Microsoft Foundry Models

cache_isolation.note: The prompt-caching guide states: "The system doesn't share prompt caches between Azure subscriptions."
cache_isolation.scope: Azure Foundry prompt-caching guide, for Microsoft Foundry Models

vulnerability_disclosure.note: The Microsoft Azure bounty programme states its scope: "Vulnerabilities submitted in the following Product(s) are eligible under this bounty program: Azure Products".
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Microsoft Azure bounty programme, for Microsoft Foundry Models

independent_audit.note: The Azure SOC 2 page states that the services in scope are listed in the attestation report and the services-in-scope page, and that page in turn points to a Service Trust Portal document behind sign-in; no public page names Foundry Models or Azure OpenAI in SOC 2 scope, so it is recorded as undocumented for the named service.
independent_audit.scope: Azure SOC 2 Type 2 compliance offering page, read for Microsoft Foundry Models

findings.claim: In 7 of these providers, we detected global cache sharing. The audit table records caching detected at the global level for an Azure text-embedding-3-small endpoint; the audits were conducted in September and early October 2024 and disclosed to each provider in October 2024.

source.label: Auditing Prompt Caching in Language Model APIs, arXiv 2502.07776v2

resolved.summary: The current prompt-caching guide states the system does not share prompt caches between Azure subscriptions; the paper does not name Azure among the providers that confirmed a change.
